implementation_statement: The patrol app provides account functions; the owner creates the 12 client portal accounts and the owner's admin account. Gap: accounts were never reviewed; 3 were stale at assessment (former retail plaza contact, an HOA A board member whose term ended, a dealership manager who left).
evidence: Patrol app user list; P07 AC-2 results
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2); Fla. Stat. 493.6118(1)(e); client agreements (confidentiality)

responsible_role: Patrol app vendor; owner assigns sites
implementation_statement: The patrol app limits each client portal account to its own site's reports and post orders. The owner assigns the site to each account.
evidence: Patrol app role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: Phone locks after 30 seconds; laptop after 10 minutes. Gap: 4-digit phone passcode and message previews on the lock screen show texted alarm codes. Owner sets a 6-digit or longer passcode and hides previews by 2026-09-15.

The phone holds the patrol app, codes in texts and a note, MFA codes, and photos. Remote locate and erase is turned on but has never been tested. Gap: no written rules for the phone; codes kept in a plain note.
The owner's only training is the Class D licensing course. The owner will complete a short small-business cybersecurity course and subscribe to monthly reminders by 2026-11-30.
The patrol app logs sign-ins, report creation and edits, and checkpoint scans with time and GPS position. The owner relies on this audit trail to show reports were not changed after submission.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; patrol app audit screen

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has reviewed the patrol app sign-in log or the email sign-in history. From 2026-10, the owner reviews both on the first Monday of each month and logs the review.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the backup agency arrangement is verbal, and the sealed code book is not yet in the safe (due 2026-09-15).
regulatory_driver: Client agreements (45-minute alarm response); Fla. Stat. 493.6121(2)

implementation_statement: The patrol app vendor backs up the platform (inherited; RPO 1 hour in its SOC 2 report). Owner responsibility: email, files, the code spreadsheet, and video have no copy outside the sync service.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; file account settings

provider_if_inherited: Patrol app vendor; device OS vendor
implementation_statement: Each client user has a named portal account; the owner does not share the admin login. Gap: the laptop has one user account shared with a family member.
evidence: Patrol app user list; laptop account settings

provider_if_inherited: Patrol app vendor; email and file provider; accounting SaaS vendor
implementation_statement: The accounting SaaS enforces MFA. Email uses text-message codes. Gap: the patrol app admin account had no MFA. The owner turns on app-based MFA for the patrol app admin account and moves email to an authenticator app by 2026-09-15.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in tests

implementation_statement: Client portal users sign in with a password only. The patrol app lets the admin require MFA for client users; the owner will tell clients and turn it on by 2026-10-31.

Passwords are remembered or saved in the browser. Gap: the patrol app admin password was reused and found in a breach list; the router admin password was the label default (both changed 2026-08-12). A password manager is planned by 2026-09-15.

The owner is the only person who can report an incident, so reporting means telling outside parties on time. Gap: no reporting times or contact list existed; the 2-hour client clause was unknown. The P08 notification matrix sets them (contacts printed by 2026-09-30).
evidence: P08 notification matrix; P07 IR-6 results
regulatory_driver: Client agreements (2-hour and 24-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(4); Fla. Stat. 493.6110(1)

implementation_statement: The ransomware runbook (P08) and notification matrix were adopted 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the runbook has not been walked through (due 2026-09-30).
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(4); client agreements (2-hour and 24-hour notice)

implementation_statement: Paper is cross-cut shredded at home. Gap: no procedure for wiping body-camera storage cards, old phones, or the laptop before disposal.

Physical access devices are client keys, access cards, and alarm and gate codes. A paper key log records each key received and returned. Gap: keys hang on one ring labeled with site names in a vehicle with no lockbox; codes are in a spreadsheet and texts; no periodic inventory; no rule to ask clients to change codes.
evidence: Key log; vehicle walkthrough; P07 PE-3 results

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-08-14 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August and after major changes (POL-01 4.3).

Vendors: patrol app vendor (and its AI model provider), email and file provider, accounting SaaS, IT technician, backup patrol agency. The patrol app vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed 2026-08-13. Gap: no vendor list; AI terms accepted without review (opt-out set 2026-08-12); no written agreement with the backup agency.

provider_if_inherited: Patrol app vendor; email and file provider
implementation_statement: The patrol app, email, and accounting SaaS use TLS (inherited). Gap: clients text alarm and gate codes by ordinary SMS, and video clips go out by public links.

The patrol app vendor encrypts data at rest; the laptop and phone are encrypted. Gap: the code spreadsheet has no protection beyond the account password, and the body-camera storage card is not encrypted.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; device settings; P07 SC-28 result
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2); Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)2. (encrypted data excluded)

provider_if_inherited: Patrol app vendor; device OS vendors; ISP
implementation_statement: The patrol app vendor patches the platform. Automatic updates are on for the laptop, phone, and patrol app; the ISP updates the router firmware.
The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

No retention schedule. Records must be kept in Florida for 2 years and produced on request (Fla. Stat. 493.6121(2)); video is kept indefinitely. POL-01 8.8 sets the schedule; first purge by 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 493.6121(2); Fla. Stat. 501.171(8); Fla. Stat. 501.171(4)(c) (5-year record)
